page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU features a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves average ratings in single-core stress-ng (1620.59) and Geekbench single-core (1635.0) tests. However, multi-core performance is weak, as demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3703.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3324.57. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with uncached read and write speeds falling into the bottom 25% and 10% categories respectively. Cryptographic and compression tasks perform at average levels, with a Passmark encryption score of 3504.96 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 25.97 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-highcpu-4 offers a dedicated compute profile with a low entry cost, though its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core limits its utility for memory-intensive workloads. It is best suited for compute-bound tasks with low memory footprints, such as single-threaded processing, basic web serving (achieving 6.78 GB/sec throughput), and lightweight utility services. It is less optimal for databases, multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale data processing due to its weak multi-core scaling and poor memory performance.
